findings.title: Initial adoption compares the serialized Context envelope to the unwrapped source payload and always rejects the ordinary Workflow consumer
findings.evidence: take_initial_executor renders expected as SourceSnapshot whose payload is the raw rules plus selected committed-context lines. The real Workflow prepare_agent instead constructs PreparedInput.payload by serde_json::to_string(&context.data). make_context wraps source.payload inside an object containing phase/workflow/generation/budget/payload. InitialWorkflowExecutor.adopt compares these different representations directly. The ordinary producer payload ends with the selected JSON-line newline, while serialized context.data is an outer JSON object without that trailing newline, so equality cannot hold even when every scope/revision/dependency is current. The failure consumes/drops the genuine preparation capability and occurs before the atomic adoption call.
findings.causal_rationale: The newly connected first-native consumer cannot adopt the real prepared namespace for Quick or Standard/Strict. This is a concrete current producer/consumer format mismatch, not missing future Sources/Gates/CLI implementation.
findings.minimal_fix: Define one canonical authoritative input representation across make_context, prepare_agent, the private initial producer and the Store proof. Compare the actual serialized envelope and its immutable phase/class/generation/budget/payload fields rather than weakening equality or replacing this gate with caller metadata. The Store comparison currently hashes context.data.payload, so coordinate that comparison with the chosen exact PreparedInput representation as well. Account for the complete rendered envelope at the existing1MiB input cap before adoption/dispatch, not just the inner source string.
causal_controls_not_executed: Use actual ManagedWorkflowSources.prepare then WorkflowEngine.initialize and the real first Executor preparation consumer with valid registered config. Verify same Unit/generation/path atomically adopted and the exact actual context envelope accepted before native input.
Mutate the inner payload, outer phase/generation/budget or persisted Context while preserving scope/revision: adoption must refuse atomically.
Use escaped UTF8/quote-heavy required content near the native input bound; measure actual serialized PreparedInput envelope and verify refusal before adoption/dispatch on overflow.

findings.title: Adoption treats the intentionally successful no-LFS grep exit1 as unresolved preparation, permanently blocking valid prepared units
findings.evidence: The adoption unsettled query rejects every helper whose receipt.exit is not string0, even when its state is confirmed/resolved. Every ordinary preparation invokes qualified_content_scoped. Its registered git grep -l LFS-pointer check intentionally accepts status1 for no matches, the usual valid repository case. UnitGit records the observed exit as string1 and marks the helper Confirmed when capture succeeds. That genuine helper row persists on the prepared unit, so the adoption query necessarily reports unsettled and refuses it. The earlier CP-M1 currently masks this independent failure on the complete consumer path.
findings.causal_rationale: Even after the payload representation is corrected, the normal healthy no-LFS preparation cannot be adopted. Known helper completion and semantic acceptance cannot be represented by a universal exit0 rule; observed source-check exit1 is not an unknown/native effect.
findings.minimal_fix: Retain conservative refusal for Pending/Unknown helpers and non-Git/native/quota effects, but use actual private producer semantic acceptance of preparation checks or an appropriate typed accepted-helper receipt. Do not globally bless arbitrary nonzero helper exits; distinguish the deliberately accepted no-match scan from rejected/unknown commands.
causal_controls_not_executed: Prepare a normal committed repository with no LFS pointer; retain the actual confirmed exit1 LFS scan row and verify the real atomic first-phase adoption succeeds once its input is valid.
Pending/Unknown helper, genuine failed mandatory source check, non-Git effect, quota lease/wait and stale authority must still reject without unit/Workflow partial mutation.
A receipt-selection omission mutant must be killed by the actual no-LFS positive and genuine unresolved negative controls separately; CP-M1 must not mask the query test.

verified_other_boundaries: Committed rule/config bytes are obtained from the actual registered tree/blob corpus at the prepared full base revision. Frame::build resolves declared tracked references within the registered Project path, hashes/parses those bytes, rejects missing/skipped/external unsupported origins, and pins Runtime native command/provider identity.

ManagedWorkflowSources.committed_input returns a private config/source/budget frame, and Workflow.inputs returns it before the legacy live load_rules fallback. The actual new ManagedWorkflowSources implementation always returns Some or errors; its error does not turn into a legacy live fallback.

The private PreparedExecutor/PreparedAdoption provenance is not deserializable. Physical namespace/clean HEAD checks precede the Immediate adoption transaction; the transaction uses exact unit authority plus Task/Project/Goal/Workflow/Context ownership and CAS and changes only unit phase/version, Workflow unit binding/version and factual audit.

First Executor phase and prior-history checks prevent later-phase reuse. Preparation abandonment remains distinct from Agent work success/artifacts. Workflow cancellation removes the retained initial source capability after actual terminal decision publication.

The retained reader source_blob command is allowed only for bounded ordinary blob OIDs returned by its exact artifact-revision tree enumeration; every helper remains journaled and epoch/artifact fenced without reopening old Task native/finalization permission.

Parent frame packing separates mandatory overhead from discretionary repo-map selection and preserves the existing hard native input cap at its downstream native consumer. The representation/cap accounting must be aligned as noted in CP-M1.

findings.title: Cached retained frame silently reuses stale governing Project/Goal instructions

evidence.detail: Retained cache rebuild is controlled only by artifact identity and revision; cached branch compares old Frame versions with artifact dependencies.
Governing execution validation runs only while prepared capability remains; after adoption it is absent.
Frame::build captures Project mandatory rule refs/config and Goal instructions into static fields.

findings.actual_guard_condition: frame.artifact/revision cache identity and frame.versions == artifact.dependencies do not validate current Project/Goal semantic instruction frame

Workflow source drift checks may accept it; a later fresh Executor reserves under the changed governing_digest but receives the old mandatory instructions. A changed Project rule ref can select another already-committed rule at the same SHA without being reflected.

verified_source_reasoning.evidence: CommittedIndex has private state, no Deserialize authority constructor, a crate-private build function, exact OID checks, and exact Task Scope checks during both selection and expansion. The production caller obtains base/revision from the registered unit or indexed retained artifact, passes that same Task scope, and does not use a live filesystem inventory as an object corpus.

verified_source_reasoning.topic: Complete inventory and compact retained dependencies
verified_source_reasoning.evidence: read_corpus uses full recursive NUL-delimited exact-commit ls-tree and exact tree-returned cat-file blob OIDs. Every entry becomes a CommittedFile; excessive inventories or failed/truncated command reads refuse. Ordinary blobs are bounded individually and in aggregate; other types and oversized files remain explicit skipped entries. The index hashes every path's OID, digest/byte count when read, and skip status into the complete sorted inventory. The producer intentionally carries that complete inventory digest, exact code SHA, rule/config digests and instruction digests into its bounded compact dependency frame rather than dropping omitted files from freshness. Retained rebuilds compare the complete compact frame against artifact dependencies.

verified_source_reasoning.topic: Normalized paths, missing content and mandatory rules
verified_source_reasoning.evidence: Index construction independently rejects non-normalized paths, traversal, Git metadata and duplicate exact paths; it does not follow filesystem aliases or perform I/O. Mandatory content and expansions must be present in readable contents and otherwise refuse with the indexed skip reason. Rule/config ingress resolves exact committed inventory entries, requires actual bytes and valid text, and rejects external or untracked origins; it does not fall back to live rule files. Distinct Git object names are lexical entries rather than claims about macOS materialized filesystem aliases.

The Frame writer counts the full serde JSON encoding including escaped text, metadata and newline bytes, with checked arithmetic, even after a budget miss; it retains no over-limit tail. Required header/mandatory/source records are counted before discretionary maps. An over-limit required frame returns NeedsBudget with no Ready slice. Optional maps are appended only if their complete encoded length fits the remaining allowance. Budget limits refer honestly to UTF-8 byte estimates, not measured provider tokens. The producer retains Goal/Task records and raw mandatory rules outside discretionary repository allocation, subtracts raw rule length plus the separating newline from its payload bound, and refuses when the complete required selected frame cannot fit. This does not qualify an entire native protocol envelope as provider-token-budgeted.

Prepared/current reads validate exact unit scope, epoch, generation and Session identity and persist a helper intent before synchronous spawn. Capture is output/time bounded and periodically fenced. Retained reads separately validate the indexed historical artifact and current reader epoch, allow exact artifact tree reads, and permit only tree-returned ordinary bounded blob OIDs; receipt completion revalidates the artifact/epoch. The Index does not mint native, Session, delegated or result-finalization authority.
